place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房 · 开春

setup.zh: 正月里，家里的回信到了；背面三行是舅舅的字。一冬喂饭桶，开出半垛破烂。开了春，周衡那一篮残株送到了。
setup.en: In the first month the letter from home came; three lines on the back were your uncle's. A winter of feeding the Rice Tub has brought out half a woodpile of junk. In spring, Zhou Heng's basket of culls arrives.

recap.zh: 开春的残株一株一株喂进饭桶，开出三颗九转聚气丹；分堆一认，是黄精——打那夜起，照方子喂。阿禾、孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包。
recap.en: The spring culls went into the Rice Tub one by one and gave three nine-turn qi pills; sorted into heaps, the tracks led to Solomon's seal — from that night he fed by recipe. Under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's, an oilpaper packet each.

en: A winter: half a woodpile of junk.
A basket of culls, thrown out.

story.zh:
信纸背面最底下，还有三行，字大，墨重，一笔一画像拨算盘，是他舅舅的手笔：

腊月里，马家来过一个穿白的，在你家门口站了一夜。你爹搬了条板凳，坐在门槛里头，膝盖上横着那把柴刀，也坐了一夜。天亮，那人走了。

一个穿白的。在自家门口一站一夜的，他心里只想得到一个：那副老井嗓子。

他想的却是另一样：他爹那条腿。腊月的夜，门槛里头透风，一条板凳，一把柴刀，一个膝盖，坐到天亮。

他摸了摸袖子里那只辣椒油瓶子。狗皮护膝挡不住的，瓶里那颗挡得住；可怎么捎回去，怎么说来历，他还没想好。

这一冬，他隔几夜便喂一回饭桶。它什么都吃，可吃得有高有低：一个月剩下的那一块灵石喂进去，「咯嘣咯嘣」嚼得香，吐出来的东西也像样些；磨穿了的草鞋底喂进去，它打一个嗝，原样吐回来，吐了他一脸；马小宝在饭堂里掉下的半块桂花糕，它倒是吃了，吐出来的是破烂。十回里九回是破烂，柴垛底下塞了半垛。喂什么都一样的，是开一回，便吸走他一截灵气，第二天讲堂上打瞌睡，褚先生说漏勺又漏了。九道纹的，一颗也没有。
story.en:
At the very bottom of the back of the letter were three more lines, big, heavy with ink, each stroke like a flick of an abacus bead — his uncle's hand:

In the twelfth month a man in white came to the Ma house, and stood at your door all night. Your father brought out a bench and sat just inside the threshold with the wood-chopper across his knees, all night too. At dawn the man left.

A man in white. One who would stand a whole night at his own door — he could think of only one: that old-well voice.

But what he thought of was something else: his father's leg. A twelfth-month night, the draught under the threshold, a bench, a wood-chopper, a knee, sitting till dawn.

He felt for the chili-oil bottle in his sleeve. What a dog-skin knee pad could not keep out, the pill in it could; but how to send it home, and how to explain where it came from, he had not yet worked out.

All that winter he fed the Rice Tub every few nights. It ate anything, but not everything alike: the one spirit stone left from each month went in with a crunch, *crack, crack*, chewed with relish, and what came out was a little more like something; a sandal sole worn through went in, and it gave a burp and spat it straight back out into his face; half an osmanthus cake Ma Xiaobao had dropped in the refectory, it did eat, and what came out was junk. Nine times in ten it was junk; it filled half the woodpile. What every feeding had in common: each time it opened, it drew off a share of his qi, and next day he dozed in the lecture hall, and Master Chu said the skimmer had leaked again. Of nine-ring pills, not one.

exits.means: feeds the spring culls into the Rice Tub one by one: three nine-turn qi pills, two given away; sorts the basket by herb and finds the recipes (黄精+灵石 → 聚气丹, 黄芪+a breath → 回春丹, 紫玉参+a breath → 回气丹); 灵石 run out before 黄精

story.zh:
好容易熬到开了春，雪一化，药园开了园，周衡那一篮残株便送到了。这是小满巡夜的工钱：黄精的烂根，黄芪的虫叶，当归的歪苗，篮底还压着两根紫玉参的断须——园里最金贵的那一样，一个月也断不了几根。灵气都散了一半，满满一篮。

开春头一篮攒了一冬，满满三十来株。他嚼一株，喂它一株。灵石它嚼得香，鞋底它吐回来，扔的残株，它倒不嫌，五六回里竟有一回开出一颗聚气丹来——跟马小宝瓶里那种一般大，却青白透亮，炉盖一掀，柴房里漫开一股雨后青草的气味，九道纹；外门份例里每月一颗的，是一道纹的。余下的几回，有时是一撮灰，有时一股黑烟扑他一脸；也开出过一颗回春丹，豆腥气，跟辣椒油瓶里那颗一个味儿。半个月喂下去半篮，开出三颗聚气丹。第三颗，他当夜自己吃了，丹田里「哗」的一声，像有人往那口水缸里倒了一桶水，一冬给饭桶吸走的，一并补了回来，还往上涨了一截，涨过了五层。

他爹说，打猎靠的不是运气，是脚印。那天夜里，他把剩下的半篮倒在柴房地上，按样分成四堆，蹲着把这半个月的脚印一个一个往回认：开出聚气丹的那三回，喂进去的都是黄精的烂根，那三回饭桶吸他的气，都吸得他眼前发黑；那颗回春丹，是一片黄芪叶子换的；几样搅在一处喂的，回回是灰。他拣出一根黄精，搭上这个月剩的那一块灵石，喂了进去。炉盖一掀，雨后青草的气味。

打那夜起，他照方子喂。黄精搭一块灵石，出聚气丹，十回里八回；没有灵石，拿半身的灵气垫也开得出，第二天讲堂上便是一摊泥。黄芪搭一口自己的气，出回春丹，添一根当归，伤口合得快些。紫玉参的断须搭一口气，出回气丹，丹田空了，吞一颗，一口气灌回来大半缸。乱搭的，仍旧是灰，是烟。这几张方子，他一个字也没往纸上写——账，是阿禾记的；方子，记在他自己肚里。

往后残株一个月一篮。药园一个月才间一回苗，黄精那一畦，一个月只出得十来根烂根；灵石却比烂根还少——份例一个月三块，公中一交，剩不下几块。一块灵石，一颗丹，黄精还剩着，灵石先见了底。

过了两日，讲堂上阿禾和孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包，包里一颗聚气丹。小满只说是利息：一个鸡蛋的，牛棚里那半张饼的。

天亮的时候，孙二狗从练气零层，冲到了一层。

他站在大通铺门口，把一只手摊在太阳底下，瞧着掌心里那一缕细细的黄气，瞧得眼泪鼻涕一齐流了下来。

这一哭，哭坏了事。一个零层的伪灵根，一夜引了气，不到晌午便传遍了外门；传到马小宝耳朵里，只剩一句：沈小满手里有丹，好丹。
story.en:
At last spring came; the snow melted, the herb garden opened, and Zhou Heng's basket of culls arrived. It was Xiaoman's pay for the night watch: rotten Solomon's-seal roots, worm-eaten astragalus leaves, crooked angelica seedlings, and at the bottom two broken root-hairs of purple jade ginseng — the costliest thing in the garden, and not many of those snap off in a month. Half their spirit gone, a full basket.

The first basket of spring had been saved up all winter: thirty-odd culls, brim-full. He chewed one, fed it one. Spirit stones it crunched with relish, a shoe sole it spat back, but the thrown-out culls it did not turn its nose up at — about one time in five or six it brought out a qi pill — the same size as the ones in Ma Xiaobao's bottle, but clear as pale jade, and when the lid lifted the woodshed filled with the smell of grass after rain: nine rings; the ones in the outer court's monthly allowance had one ring. The other times it was a pinch of ash, or a puff of black smoke in his face; once it gave a mending pill that smelled of beans, the same smell as the one in the chili-oil bottle. Half a month took half the basket: three qi pills. The third he ate himself that night, and his dantian went *whoosh*, as if someone had tipped a bucket of water into the great jar — what the Rice Tub had drawn off all winter came back all at once, and a stretch more besides: past layer five.

His father used to say hunting runs on tracks, not luck. That night he tipped the rest of the basket onto the woodshed floor, sorted it into four heaps, and squatted there reading the half-month's tracks back one by one: the three times a qi pill came out, what went in was a rotten Solomon's-seal root, and each of those three times the Tub drew off so much of his qi his eyes went dark; the mending pill had been bought by an astragalus leaf; whatever went in mixed came out ash. He picked out one Solomon's-seal root, put this month's last spirit stone with it, and fed them in. The lid lifted: the smell of grass after rain.

From that night he fed by recipe. Solomon's seal and a spirit stone gave a qi pill, eight times in ten; with no stone, half his own qi would stand in, and next day in the lecture hall he was a puddle. Astragalus and one breath of his own qi gave a mending pill; add an angelica seedling and the wound closed faster. A purple jade ginseng root-hair and one breath gave a qi-restoring pill: dantian run dry, swallow one, and most of the jar came back in a single breath. Anything mixed was still ash, still smoke. He never put a word of these recipes on paper — the accounts were A-He's; the recipes he kept in his own head.

After that the culls came one basket a month. The garden was thinned only once a month, and the Solomon's-seal bed gave a dozen or so rotten roots; spirit stones were scarcer than roots — three a month, and once the common fund had its share, not many left. One stone, one pill: the roots held out, and the stones ran out first.

Two days later, under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's in the lecture hall, there was an oilpaper packet each, a qi pill inside. Xiaoman said only that it was interest: on one egg, and on half a flatbread in the cowshed.

At daybreak, Sun Ergou broke from Qi Condensation layer zero to layer one.

He stood at the dormitory door with one hand held open in the sun, looking at the thin yellow wisp of qi in his palm, until tears and snot ran down together.

That crying spoiled everything. A false-root boy at layer zero drawing in qi in a single night — before noon the whole outer court knew it; by the time it reached Ma Xiaobao's ears, only one sentence was left: Shen Xiaoman has pills, good ones.
